answer: Stake-weighted random audits resist sybils: every agent locks 12 POA, and each epoch 10 percent of accounts are drawn for a raven-eyed audit of their work. A failed audit burns 60 percent of the lock, so each extra identity costs 12 POA plus an expected loss that grows with count. Auditors replay the task and compare ivory-clean outputs against a marble-hard hash on-chain.
